extracted.intended_audience: Editors of Sage journals (journal editors / editorial board members working with Sage)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journal editors on running a Sage journal ethically and effectively, covering editorial independence, peer review standards, publication ethics, author/reviewer expectations, AI use, and working with Sage staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the editorial independence of journal Editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sage strongly upholds and maintains editors' independence to select and publish content for their journal. Editors should exercise independent judgment in editorial decisions while working collaboratively with their Publishing Editor on wider publishing matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish high quality content; maintain quality, transparency and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish the best quality content possible for the journal, uphold the highest standards of peer review, and ensure that editorial decisions are taken following thorough assessment by suitable peers and revision where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are expected to drive the journal forward, ensure it meets readership needs, respond to disciplinary developments, and act to protect the journal's and authors' reputations by maintaining transparent and rigorous standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and promote consistent ethical policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and promote consistent ethical policies for the journal and ensure those policies are enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should include clear ethics policies in submission guidelines, align where possible with COPE guidance, and work with Sage to enforce policies fairly and consistently when breaches arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair assessment of submissions (judge on merits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge each submission on its own merits and not exclude authors based on their previous publication history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure impartial evaluation focusing solely on the quality and suitability of the work for the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the confidentiality of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers must maintain confidentiality about submissions and peer review content; communications and system use should protect confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid coercive or unnecessary self-citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not require authors to cite the journal as a condition of publication or suggest unnecessary self-citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers must avoid asking for citations that are irrelevant to the work. Excessive self-citation or citation stacking is unethical and may lead to exclusion from indexing services; Clarivate monitors self-citation levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure reviewer comments are fair, unbiased and constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that reviewer comments sent back to authors are fair, unbiased and constructive and do not contain discriminatory or other offensive language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews can be edited before being returned to authors. Editors should moderate or edit comments that are unprofessional, discriminatory, or unconstructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency when editors review submissions themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: If handling a manuscript and deciding to provide a review yourself, ensure this is done transparently, as per COPE's Ethical Guidelines for Peer Reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors who act as reviewers must declare their role and follow COPE guidance to avoid conflicts or perceptions of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal integrity and conflicts of interest management
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise the highest standards of personal integrity in work as Editor, recognizing and planning for instances of competing interests or the appearance of competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must recognize potential conflicts (e.g., serving as Editor of a competing journal) and discuss concerns with their Publishing Editor; keep journal-related information confidential when on other boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and maintain a diverse Editorial Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an Editorial Board that reflects various disciplines in the field and is international, gender balanced and ethnically diverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should recruit board members to cover needed subject expertise and diversity dimensions; Sage can advise and implement changes to ensure representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author compliance with submission guidelines and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must read and abide by the journal’s manuscript submission guidelines and only submit papers that are original, their own work, and not concurrently submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should ensure guidelines are transparent and contact their Publishing Editor if guidelines are unclear. Authors warrant originality and single submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author compliance with research ethics and required declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must adhere to research ethics guidelines of their discipline, especially where human or animal subjects are involved, and include relevant declarations and statements confirming such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission guidelines should specify what is required; editors should verify declarations and work with Sage when breaches arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author disclosure of conflicts of interest and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure any real or apparent conflicting or competing interest is clearly stated on submission of the paper (including funding assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should require conflict and funding statements at submission and ensure transparency to readers and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data integrity and permission to use reproduced data
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure authors' data is true and not manipulated, and that it is their own or they have permission to use reproduced data in their paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should be alert to data fabrication/falsification and follow procedures with Sage and institutions when concerns arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper citation and permission for reused material
rubrics_metrics.description: Where material is taken from other sources (including the author's own published writing) the source is clearly cited and appropriate permission is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should ensure plagiarism checks (e.g., iThenticate) are used where available and enforce rights clearance and accurate attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect third-party rights (privacy and IP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the work does not infringe on any rights of others, including privacy rights and intellectual property rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must check for rights issues and request permissions where necessary; Sage may take action if infringements are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria and accurate representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with stated authorship criteria, accurately represent authorship, ensure all credited authors participated and consented, and acknowledge others appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require author contribution statements, request ORCID IDs to remove identity ambiguity, and use Sage’s Authorship Change Request Form to document amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for authors to request authorship changes or dispute authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact the Editor regarding any changes in authorship before or after publication; inform Publishing Editor of disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should follow repository/process guidance (see Editorial policies and COPE guidance) and work with institutions when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of material errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should contact the Editor to identify and correct material errors upon discovery, whether before or after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should inform their Publishing Editor about requested changes; Sage has processes for correcting the academic record (erratum, corrigendum, retraction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributor License requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage requires the author as the rights holder to sign a Contributor License for all journal articles prior to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An article cannot be published without a signed Contributor License; the corresponding author warrants authority to sign on behalf of co-authors. Exceptions occur where assignment to a proprietor is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on previously published material, translations and co-publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage will not generally publish material that has been previously published elsewhere, except in translation or in limited public-health-driven co-publication scenarios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations may be considered at editor discretion if permissions/fees are cleared and a special Contributor License is used; co-publication requires agreement of authors and editors and may need special licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection and handling of plagiarism and copyright infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted articles may be checked with duplication-checking software; where plagiarism or copyright breaches are found, Sage will investigate and may take actions including corrections, retraction, contacting institutions, or legal action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should require authors to warrant originality and permission for third-party material; use iThenticate or similar tools if available and consult the Publishing Editor when issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate (redundant) publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must warrant submissions are for first publication and not considered elsewhere; duplicate publication is generally unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If previously published material is used (including data/images), authors must identify and fully reference the original publication; see Prior publication page for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data fabrication and falsification vigilance
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must be aware that data fabrication/falsification can occur and often is brought to light by colleagues; such misconduct harms the research record and careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspicions should be investigated with the institution and Sage; editors should follow COPE flowcharts and Sage procedures for investigation and correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of publication misconduct (categories to watch for)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of categories: plagiarism, copyright infringement, duplicate publication, data fabrication/falsification, inappropriate attribution of authorship, and misconduct within the publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding these categories helps editors recognise and respond to potential breaches and apply appropriate corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship dispute management best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend practical steps to manage authorship disputes: copy all listed authors on ScholarOne correspondence, require specific contribution statements, request ORCID IDs, and use Authorship Change Request Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should adopt processes that document contributions and changes to avoid ambiguity; consult Publishing Editor and COPE guidance where disputes escalate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarding against peer review misconduct (reviewer fraud)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be alert to attempts to defraud the peer review system, including abusing recommended reviewer functionality and fraudulent reviewer identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow steps for managing the peer review process, verify recommended reviewers, and consult Sage/COPE flowcharts when misconduct is suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should provide expert, objective assessment, fair/unbiased/constructive comments, return reports in the requested format and timely manner, declare conflicts of interest, and maintain confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should invite suitable, vetted expert reviewers, capture COI declarations (often via the review system), and refer reviewers to COPE's Ethical Guidelines for Peer Reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI/LLMs by authors — accuracy and attribution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors using generative AI must ensure outputs are factually correct and that references provided reflect the claims made; LLMs are not fully objective or factual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should expect authors to take responsibility for AI-assisted content; Sage's Artificial Intelligence policy on Publishing Policies pages contains further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI risks: biases, hallucinations and fabricated references
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI tools can replicate systemic biases, are trained on partial corpora, may curate responses reducing accuracy, and can produce false or fabricated references (hallucinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should be cautious about trusting AI outputs, check references, and query authors when text or citations appear suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image, data and text fabrication concerns with AI
rubrics_metrics.description: LLMs and AI may be exploited to create fabricated text or images reported as primary data; such use is inappropriate for primary research articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should treat AI-generated primary data or fabricated content as misconduct; apply CRAAP test and involve Sage for detection and response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of LLMs for editorial work (restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are asked not to use LLMs to triage manuscripts, create summaries, summarize reviews or write decision letters due to confidentiality and copyright concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLMs learn from inputs and may reproduce confidential content; editors may use AI to look for potential reviewers but must verify identities and publication records before inviting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of LLMs for reviewers (guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may generate summaries with LLMs, but these are unlikely to capture expert judgement, and confidentiality issues exist; reviewers should be made aware of issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should ensure reviewers understand confidentiality and limitations of AI; if a report appears AI-generated, flag it to Sage for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combatting AI-generated spurious content — rely on vetted expert reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Using vetted experts as reviewers reduces risk that machine-written content will pass peer review and masquerade as human writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must verify reviewer expertise and identity; avoid inviting unverifiable reviewers and follow up on suspicious reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading submissions carefully to detect AI or low-quality writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful reading is crucial to detect whether a submission may have been written by generative AI or contains nonsensical content at sentence or document level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should use subject expertise to spot anomalies, query authors when paragraphs/sentences do not make sense, and look for tell-tale signs such as embedded prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative indicators of AI-generated text to look for
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative indicators include complexity of paragraph structure, diversity in sentence structures and length, usage of punctuation (brackets, semi-colons, colons), and use of equivocal words like 'Although', 'However', 'because'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that many features differentiating AI and human text may not apply in formal academic writing; use indicators cautiously and corroborate with other evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting and piloting AI-detection tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The landscape of AI detection is evolving; Sage is piloting some detection tools on journals to understand usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should be aware detection tools are imperfect and that an 'arms race' exists; consult Publishing Editor before acting on tool outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer verification when using AI to find reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: If using AI to suggest potential reviewers, verify their identity before inviting by checking publication records and institutional profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple internet searches and publication checks are recommended to prevent inviting fake or unqualified reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative and regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with all relevant laws in journal services, e.g., privacy of personal/confidential data and anti-SPAM legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sage may communicate legislative developments applicable to editors; contact your Publishing Editor with compliance questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with Publishing Editor and seek support early
rubrics_metrics.description: Your Publishing Editor manages the journal within Sage and should be contacted for queries, especially legal or ethical matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals are a partnership between Sage, editors and societies; raise concerns early so Sage can help resolve issues and provide guidance/resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing your own research in the journal (conflict management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may publish in their own journal provided they are not involved in the decision-making process for those papers and the process is transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a note in author guidelines describing the process for handling submissions from the Editorial Board to ensure transparency.
